operations.body: Added from "Review the board for use by several people at once" on 2026-11-21, as part of this story's scope. When the board is hosted (a public address is set), its answers must not carry the server's folder, the remote's address or Git's own output. Today a failed publication of a status, priority, key or display change answers with Git's error text, for example "fatal: '/srv/.../missing.git' does not appear to be a git repository". A hosted board answers with a short sentence and writes the detail to the server's own log with an id that ties the two together. A person's own local board keeps the full detail. Stripping credentials from Git's output (PR #209) cannot cover a credential helper's own output or a token in an address's path or query, so this is the complete protection. The hosting answers also set caching headers suited to a shared machine (attachments and task pages are private and not stored).
